report:
# DS-QM102-SYNDROME-CAPACITY-BOUND

The distance formula is tested on actual odd repetition codes {0^n,1^n}. Every error is enumerated, with adjacent-XOR syndrome and majority correction; all weight<=t errors correct the transmitted zero word. The all-ones logical error has zero syndrome and is uncorrected. This is a declared classical code control, not a stabilizer/homology classification.

Supported: Complete retained repetition-code error tables and zero-syndrome logical controls are exact; the distance arithmetic and three-bit correction statement are kernel checked.

Remaining: Prove the arbitrary code/homology distance and decoder transport under the actual error model. A guaranteed-correctable lower bound is not a universal upper-bound theorem.
